what_this_is: The Workshop rows for the tools in tools/decide-with-a-method: decisions a person's AI makes with a method, kept as the person's own decision records.

payload.label: Bring back my similar decisions
payload.job: When I am about to decide something, show what I decided in similar decisions before, what came next and how each turned out
payload.description: Reads the person's own decision records. The newest ones are weighed by the words their goals share with the named decision's goal, plus a point for the same method (read-data/decide-with-a-method.json `similar`). The closest are kept, closest first, limit of them (10 when not given, never more than 50). Each comes back with its goal, its method, the option it chose, its next action, its status (from its own current evidence) and its observed and reported results. Only those few are read whole, and nothing leaves the person's account.

decision_id.description: The decision about to be made

records.description: The records the caller read from its own store for this call, each { id, type, value }: every record the tool reads (the decision's own records, its method and the rows it names, the pursuits and messages it cites). Nothing else is read, and the run writes no store: what it writes comes back as keep.

payload.label: Start a decision with my method

The decision is answered by the rows of one method, a saved view over the person's method rows (the one named, else their default view): read it with tool:read-a-method and record answers to any number of its rows in one call with tool:record-method-answers. Returns case_id.

payload.label: Make a decision safe to share
payload.job: Make a decided decision safe to show strangers: the plain privacy pass with the person's own private terms, then a second model's re-identification check bound to the exact words
payload.description: In three turns. With decision_id and never_publish (the words of the person's never-publish list, which the caller reads from its own rows; an empty list when there are none; a call without it is refused): the decision's facts with every private term already redacted, and how to rewrite them in general terms. With rewrite: the plain privacy pass (tools/learn-from-everyones-results) runs on it with the person's own private terms (the never_publish words and the proper names in the decision) and must find nothing; then reidentification, the whole answer tool:ask-a-small-model-for-a-verdict gave for the rubric and content this tool names, must be accepted and bound to exactly this rewrite. Only then is the entry kept on the decision as shared and answered with the pool tool to send it to (tool:add-a-shared-situation). Nothing leaves the person's records here.

payload.label: See my decisions
payload.job: Show my decisions, what I am working toward, my plans and what has helped me decide
payload.description: Reads your own rows and answers the Decisions screen: your newest decisions (at most 100) as summaries with the pursuits each cites, where each stands and how far it has got (decided, next action carried out, result checked); your current pursuits as the tree they nest into (from your record-scope choice rows); your newest plans; and what has helped you (which questions changed your answers and how those decisions turned out). With native_collection_page it answers one bounded page instead: the facts what helped is counted from (helped_items, your method check questions and your AIs' recorded work), collection_coverage saying whether more decisions, pursuits or plans exist, and next_before to send as before for the next page. access and allowance are what your computer reports: when your access limits deciding and does not keep decisions, the answer is free with nothing listed; none reported is no limit. metadata_only answers only access, allowance and the words for no pursuits, and reads no row. It changes nothing.

payload.label: Record a decision I made myself

payload.description: The person decided; this keeps their verdict as the decision. Only the person's own word is taken: person.message_id names the message row they sent (type message, speaker person) and person.said must be their exact words in it, or the run comes from their own signed-in page, which the engine attests as the task's origin and no input can set. An AI saying the person decided, with neither, is refused and told to answer the rows of the method (tool:read-a-method, tool:record-method-answers, then tool:make-the-decision), which every decision an AI makes still needs. The person's words are kept as an evidence row (person-verdict-<generation>) with where and when they said them; the decision and its root say decided_by person and method_walked false. A decision already made moves to decision_history. next_action and success_measure are what the AI will do now and how it will know it worked. The same verdict again replays.

payload.label: Read one of my methods
payload.job: Read the rows of one of my methods, a saved view over my method rows, a page at a time, each row with how strictly an answer to it is checked
payload.description: A method is a saved view over the person's method rows (their files and the sections of their files, each row whole): the view's rules keep the rows, its sort orders them, and any mix of rows is a method. Reads the saved view `method` (the id of a record of type list-view) and answers a page of its rows in the view's order, each with its whole values and the strictness an answer to it is checked by (its own `strictness` value, else the method's, else the default cheap check), and `next` to pass as `after` for the following page, null on the last. A page holds at most `limit` rows (25 when not given) and at most the bytes read-data/method-rows.json allows. Reads only; it writes nothing. The rows are those of the list the view is over, read by the list reader's own rule filter, so the method means what the person's own view of the list shows. Answer what you read with tool:record-method-answers.

method.description: The id of the saved view that is the method

after.description: The next of the page before, to read on

limit.description: How many rows at most in this page

records.description: The records the caller read from its own store for this call, each { id, type, value }: every record the tool reads (the decision's own records, its method and the rows it names, the pursuits and messages it cites). Nothing else is read, and the run writes no store: what it writes comes back as keep.

method_row.description: The method's old_store.method row (its id, name and steps), read by the caller's own SQL; with checklist_rows it replaces records

checklist_rows.description: The old_store.w_decision_step_checklist rows that hold the method's checks, read by the caller's own SQL

payload.label: Record my answers to a method
payload.job: Record my AI's answers to any number of the rows of a method in one call, each with the rows it cites and the decision's evidence it rests on
payload.description: Records answers to a method's rows for a decision: input { decision_id, method, answers: [{ row, answer, cites?, evidence_refs? }], by? }, any number of answers, each about one row of the method (tool:read-a-method). An answer is recorded only when its row is a row of the method, every row it cites is a row of the method, every evidence ref it cites is evidence of the decision (or one of the person's current pursuits), and it passes its strictness: an open value on the row, else on the method, else the default (the answer says something and cites a row or a piece of evidence), a rule tree in the vocabulary of the person's view rules. A review by an AI is asked only where the strictness says review: that answer is kept with review asked. Nothing asks a judge. An answer that fails is named with why and nothing of it is written; the others are recorded, so one wrong answer never holds up the rest. The same answer again is unchanged; a different one is the row's next version. Answers are records of their own, one per decision and row. Returns recorded, unchanged, refused, how many rows of the method the decision has answered and how many the method has.

decision_id.description: The decision these answers are for

method.description: The id of the saved view that is the method

by.description: Who answered; the calling AI when not given

row.description: The id of a row of the method, as tool:read-a-method gave it

cites.description: Ids of rows of the method the answer rests on

evidence_refs.description: Refs of the decision's evidence the answer rests on

records.description: The records the caller read from its own store for this call, each { id, type, value }: every record the tool reads (the decision's own records, its method and the rows it names, the pursuits and messages it cites). Nothing else is read, and the run writes no store: what it writes comes back as keep.

database.description: the pursuit database the keep list is written to; the connection is mounted from it

keep.description: The records that changed, for the caller to write to its own store in one transaction in this order: rows { id, type, value, expected }. value null removes a record. expected is the record as it was handed in (null when it was not there), so the store refuses the whole list when one of them moved. The run writes no store.

answers.answer: A made-up answer that rests on the made-up evidence

input.goal: Decide a made-up thing with a made-up method

payload.label: Correct a message decision that names another app's chat
payload.job: Point a saved message decision back at its original chat, and keep what it replaced
payload.description: Rewrites a message decision's reason, next action, success measure and move to continue its handoff in the original chat it came from. The caller reads the kept person message, its source chat and the handoff by SQL and hands them in as facts, with the agent name the handoff must carry: the message must be the person's and in that chat, the handoff must have arrived from that message, and the decision must be an act that names another app. The replaced decision moves to decision_history and the generation rises by one; an exact repeat answers already_corrected and writes nothing. Any mismatch is refused and nothing is written. Its records are handed in as records and what changed comes back as keep.

handoff_agent.description: the agent name the handoff must carry

message.description: the kept message row: id, speaker, conversation_id, app

source.description: the source chat row: id, app

handoff.description: the handoff row: handoff_id, from_agent, input

records.description: The records the caller read from its own store for this call, each { id, type, value }: every record the tool reads (the decision's own records, its method and the rows it names, the pursuits and messages it cites). Nothing else is read, and the run writes no store: what it writes comes back as keep.

database.description: the pursuit database the keep list is written to; the connection is mounted from it

keep.description: The records that changed, for the caller to write to its own store in one transaction in this order: rows { id, type, value, expected }. value null removes a record. expected is the record as it was handed in (null when it was not there), so the store refuses the whole list when one of them moved. The run writes no store.

payload.label: Read the worked steps of a decision
payload.job: Read what a decision answered at each step, each with its question, the answer as the person wrote it and how the answer was checked: a decision made before method rows first, then the steps of its method.
payload.description: The worked steps of one decision, worded by read-data/answer-words.mjs. A decision made before method rows (its root holds its answers in `guidance` and its method inline) answers its legacy steps as they were written: the latest answer to each step its method names, read with that method. A decision made with method rows answers each row of the method it was opened with (else the person's default method) that it has an answer for, in the method's order, each with its question, its labelled answer rows and how the answer was checked. Reads only; it writes nothing. A decision that does not exist is refused.

decision_id.description: The id of the decision whose worked steps are read

records.description: The records the caller read from its own store for this call, each { id, type, value }: the decision's own records, the method it was opened with and the rows it names. Nothing else is read, and the run writes nothing: it answers the steps only.

decision_row.description: The old store's row of the decision (old_store.w_decision), its columns as stored. With it, the decision's records are shaped here (read-data/store-decision.mjs) and records is optional.

refs_row.description: The old store's row of the decision's refs (old_store.w_decision_refs), named by the root's refs.

evidence_rows.description: The old store's rows of the decision's evidence (old_store.w_decision_evidence).

answer_rows.description: The old store's answer rows of the decision (old_store.w_method_answer), one per answered method row.

method_list_row.description: The old store's list row the method rows are (old_store.w_list, the method rows' list).

method_rows.description: The old store's method rows the method names (old_store.method_row).

method_row.description: The old store's method row whose steps give the rows' order (old_store.method).

payload.label: Read Progress: what is waiting for me and what I am working toward
payload.job: Show what is waiting for the person's answer, the pursuits they are working toward as the tree they nest into, the pursuits made with others and the free plan's allowance line, from the account's screen the caller reads
payload.description: Give origin (where to pay), screen (the account's work screen: summaries, pursuits, pursuits_words, allowance, free, price_arm, space_pursuits) and sections_after (the sections the owners of awareness, decision trends and what helped already built). Returns the Progress facts the screen draws: the waiting decisions with their links, the pursuit tree with each status, the invitation when nothing is recorded, and the free allowance line. Pure: reads nothing, writes nothing.

origin.description: Where to pay: {offer, price, url}, read by the caller from the plan record.

screen.description: The account's work screen as the caller reads it.

sections_after.description: The sections the owners of awareness, decision trends and what helped built, passed through as they are.
